senses.definition: A vegetable with leaves that may be curly or flat and are eaten cooked or raw.
senses.example: We tore the kale into small pieces for the salad.

senses.definition: A tube with mirrors inside that makes changing colorful patterns when you look through it and turn it.
senses.example: I twisted the kaleidoscope until the red pieces formed a star.

senses.definition: An Australian animal with strong back legs for hopping; a mother carries her young in a pouch.
senses.example: The kangaroo crossed the open grass in long hops.

senses.definition: A type of exercise and sport from Japan that teaches controlled movements such as kicks and blocks.
senses.example: We practiced balance and careful steps at our first karate lesson.

senses.definition: An insect related to a grasshopper, with long feelers and often wings that look like leaves.
senses.example: We heard a katydid call from the garden at dusk.

senses.definition: A narrow boat moved using a paddle with a blade at each end.
senses.example: Our kayak slid quietly past the tall reeds.

senses.definition: To travel in a kayak.
senses.example: We kayaked around the island on a calm morning.

senses.definition: A strong part along the bottom of a ship or boat that helps support it or keep it steady.
senses.example: The model sailboat had a heavy keel below the water.

senses.definition: Very interested in something or eager to do it.
senses.example: Sofia is keen to try the new climbing wall.

senses.definition: Especially sharp or strong, as a sense or feeling can be.
senses.example: The fox used its keen hearing to find a mouse under the snow.

senses.definition: To hold on to something rather than give it away or lose it.
senses.example: You can keep the card you made.

senses.definition: To stay in one state or help someone or something stay that way.
senses.example: The blanket kept us warm during the game.

senses.definition: To continue or do something again and again.
senses.example: Keep stirring until the batter is smooth.

senses.definition: To watch someone or something and be ready to notice a change or problem.
senses.example: Please keep an eye on the cookies while I set the table.

senses.definition: To notice and remember what happens to someone or something over time, often by making a record.
senses.example: I use a notebook to keep track of the seeds that sprout.

senses.definition: Something you keep to remember a person, place, or event.
senses.example: I saved a ticket from our first train trip as a keepsake.

senses.definition: A kind of large brown seaweed.
senses.example: Fish hid under the long kelp blades.

senses.definition: A small shelter for a dog, or a place where dogs are cared for while their people are away.
senses.example: Pepper stayed at a kennel during our trip.

senses.definition: A tough material your body makes for parts such as hair, nails, and the outer layer of skin.
senses.example: Your fingernails contain keratin.

senses.definition: The inner or edible part of a seed or nut, or one grain of corn.
senses.example: The last kernel of popcorn popped in the pan.

senses.definition: A thick sauce usually made from tomatoes, vinegar, and seasonings.
senses.example: I dipped a potato wedge in ketchup.

senses.definition: A container with a lid and often a spout, used to heat water.
senses.example: Dad turned off the kettle when it began to whistle.

senses.definition: A small tool used to open or close a lock.
senses.example: I used the key to open our front door.

senses.definition: One of the buttons on a keyboard or another instrument.
senses.example: Press the space key to pause the video.

senses.definition: Especially important to what happens next.
senses.example: Filling the water bottles was a key part of getting ready.

senses.definition: To enter letters or numbers using buttons or a keyboard, often said as “key in.”
senses.example: The librarian keyed in my card number.

senses.definition: A set of buttons you press to enter letters, numbers, or commands.
senses.example: I used the keyboard to type my name.

senses.definition: A musical instrument with a row of keys, or the row of keys itself.
senses.example: Yara played the same tune on an electronic keyboard.

senses.definition: A small opening in a lock into which a key fits.
senses.example: The room was so dim I could hardly see the keyhole.

senses.definition: A ring that keeps several keys together.
senses.example: She slipped the new key onto her keyring.

senses.definition: The center stone at the top of an arch that helps hold the arch in place.
senses.example: We could see the keystone at the very top of the bridge arch.

senses.definition: A kind of living thing that has an especially large effect on the other living things around it.
senses.example: A sea star can be a keystone species when it keeps mussels from taking up most of the space on a shore.

senses.definition: To hit someone or something with your foot, or swing your leg as if to do so.
senses.example: Rae kicked the ball to the far side of the field.

senses.definition: A hit or motion made with the foot.
senses.example: A strong kick sent the ball over the fence.

senses.definition: A game in which players kick a ball and run around bases.
senses.example: We played kickball in the yard during lunch.

senses.definition: A child or young person.
senses.example: Chloe was the first kid in the class to finish the mural.

senses.definition: A young goat.
senses.example: The kid stayed close to its mother in the pen.

senses.definition: To joke, often by saying something you do not really mean.
senses.example: I was kidding when I said that my backpack could talk.

senses.definition: One of the body parts that clean the blood and make urine from some waste and extra water.
senses.example: A kidney can return water to the blood after filtering it.

senses.definition: An oven that gets very hot, used for heating clay pots and other materials.
senses.example: A grown-up put the dry clay bowls into the kiln.

senses.definition: A unit for an amount of electrical energy equal to one kilowatt of power used for one hour.
senses.example: The bill showed how many kilowatt-hours the building had used.

senses.definition: Caring about how others feel and trying to help them.
senses.example: It was kind of you to bring a towel for your teammate.

senses.definition: A group of things that share certain features.
senses.example: What kind of apple did we plant?

senses.definition: To start a fire, or to cause a feeling or interest to start.
senses.example: The dinosaur display kindled my interest in fossils.

senses.definition: Small sticks or other dry material used to help start a fire.
senses.example: The ranger set out a small bundle of kindling.

senses.definition: A form of “kindle” that means starting to burn or beginning to create a feeling.
senses.example: Her jokes were kindling a small spark of hope in the group.

senses.definition: In a friendly, caring, or helpful way.
senses.example: The bus driver spoke kindly to the nervous passenger.

senses.definition: A caring or helpful action, or the quality of caring about others.
senses.example: It was a kindness to walk home with the new student.

senses.definition: A male ruler in a country with a royal family, or a card or game piece with that name.
senses.example: The king in the story asked a gardener to design the palace grounds.

senses.definition: A country or area ruled by a king or queen.
senses.example: In the story, the lost traveler wandered into a new kingdom.

senses.definition: A broad group used by scientists to sort living things.
senses.example: Mushrooms belong to the kingdom called fungi.

senses.definition: A bird often seen near water, known for diving to catch small fish or other animals.
senses.example: A kingfisher perched on a low branch over the pond.

senses.definition: A sharp twist or bend, especially in a rope, tube, or wire.
senses.example: A kink in the hose kept water from coming out.

senses.definition: To twist into or cause a sharp bend.
senses.example: The wire kinked when I bent it around the corner.

senses.definition: A small booth or stand that sells things, gives information, or has a screen people can use.
senses.example: A kiosk near the park gate sold maps and postcards.

senses.definition: A set of things to use for a particular job or activity.
senses.example: My art kit has pencils, a ruler, and an eraser.

senses.definition: A room or area where food is prepared and cooked.
senses.example: Our soup simmered in the kitchen while we set the table.

senses.definition: A young cat.
senses.example: The kitten chased a piece of string under the chair.

senses.definition: A small fruit with brownish skin and green or golden flesh containing tiny black seeds.
senses.example: I scooped the center of the kiwifruit out with a spoon.

senses.definition: To work dough by pressing, folding, and stretching it.
senses.example: We kneaded the dough until it felt smooth.

senses.definition: The part in the middle of your leg where it bends.
senses.example: I put a bandage on my knee after I fell.

senses.definition: The small round bone at the front of the knee.
senses.example: The doctor pointed to the kneecap in the drawing.

senses.definition: To go down onto one or both knees.
senses.example: We knelt by the pool to watch the tadpoles swim.

senses.definition: A tool with a handle and a blade, often used for cutting.
senses.example: I used a kitchen knife to slice the bread with Dad's help.

senses.definition: In earlier times in parts of Europe, a trained warrior who often rode a horse and served a ruler. In some places today, knighthood is a special honor.
senses.example: The museum displayed a knight’s old suit of armor.

senses.definition: The chess piece shaped like a horse’s head. It moves two squares in a straight line and then one square at a right angle.
senses.example: The knight can jump over another piece on the chessboard.

senses.definition: To make cloth by joining loops of yarn, often with needles.
senses.example: My aunt is knitting a yellow scarf.

senses.definition: A rounded part that you turn, pull, or hold.
senses.example: I turned the knob to lower the oven temperature.

senses.definition: To hit something, often quickly or by accident.
senses.example: I knocked my elbow against the table.

senses.definition: To tap on a door to let someone inside know you are there.
senses.example: Please knock before you come into my room.

senses.definition: A sound made by a hit or tap.
senses.example: I heard a knock just as I closed my book.

senses.definition: A small rounded hill.
senses.example: We could see the town from the grassy knoll.

senses.definition: A tight loop made by tying rope, string, or similar material.
senses.example: We tied a knot at the end of the jump rope.

senses.definition: A hard, round mark in wood where a branch used to grow.
senses.example: You can see a knot in the middle of this board.

senses.definition: To have learned or understood something so that you can remember or use it.
senses.example: I know how to count by sixes.

senses.definition: To be familiar with a person, place, or thing from experience.
senses.example: Do you know the people who live next door?

senses.definition: Knowing a lot about a subject.
senses.example: The knowledgeable guide could name every tree along the trail.

senses.definition: One of the joints in your fingers, especially the bumps you see when you close your hand.
senses.example: A little paint dried on my knuckle.

senses.definition: An Australian animal with round ears that spends much of its time in trees and mainly eats eucalyptus leaves.
senses.example: The koala clung to a branch with its eyes closed.

senses.definition: Small swimming animals with bodies shaped a little like tiny shrimp.
senses.example: A whale took in a mouthful of water full of krill.
